hero.lead: A nation of 2.6 million with forest over nine tenths of its land, which returned to the Eurobond market in 2026 while it audits a public debt of 70% or more of GDP.

record.text: Seven-year Eurobond: 9.375% amortising notes due 2033, priced 30 July 2026; final offering circular published 6 August 2026
Public debt, share of GDP, 2024, projected by the IMF to reach 94.3% in 2027
World Bank financing for piped water, electricity and safely managed sanitation for about 535,000 people, approved 5 February 2026

register.name: Eurobond due 2034
register.detail: US$580 million · 9.375% amortising notes due 21 October 2034 · Offering circular published 19 October 2026
register.note: Gabon’s second Eurobond of 2026, after the notes due 2033
register.text: The Gabonese Republic’s second international bond of 2026: US$580 million of 9.375% amortising notes due 21 October 2034. It carries the same coupon as the notes due 2033.

register.name: Eurobond due 2033
register.detail: US$920 million · 9.375% amortising notes due 2033 · Pricing announced 30 July 2026 · Final offering circular published 6 August 2026
register.note: Gabon’s return to the Eurobond market in 2026
register.text: US$920 million of 9.375% amortising notes due 2033, with which the Gabonese Republic returned to the international bond market in 2026. Its coupon of 9.375% is the price of market borrowing for the nation in 2026.

register.name: CEMAC public bond, EOG 2025 à tranches multiples 2
register.detail: First listed on the BVMAC 18 May 2026 · 10,647,876 bonds of FCFA 10,000 · Tranche A 5.6% net, 2025–2027 · Tranche B 6% net, 2025–2028
register.note: 8,521,635 bonds in tranche A and 2,126,241 in tranche B
register.text: A bond of the Gabonese State sold by public offering in the Central African Economic and Monetary Community and listed on the regional stock exchange, the BVMAC, in Douala. Borrowing in CFA francs within the region avoids exchange-rate risk for the State, at 5.6% and 6% net, against 9.375% on its 2026 dollar bonds.

register.name: Debt conversion for ocean conservation (blue bond)
register.detail: Announced 14 August 2023 · US$500 million of Eurobonds due 2025, February 2031 and November 2031 bought back · Blue loan funded by Gabon Blue Bond Master Trust notes · DFC political risk insurance of up to $500 million
register.note: An expected $163 million of new funding for ocean conservation
register.text: The first debt conversion for marine conservation in mainland Africa, according to The Nature Conservancy: US$500 million of Gabon’s bonds were refinanced with a blue loan funded by blue bonds arranged by Bank of America and insured by the DFC. It frees $5 million a year for 15 years for ocean conservation, builds an endowment expected to reach about $88 million by 2038, and supports a marine protected area network rising from 26% to 30% of Gabon’s ocean.

register.name: Food sovereignty investment conventions
register.detail: Signed 4 May 2026, Libreville · Five conventions · Ministers of the Economy and of Agriculture
register.text: Five conventions worth more than XOF 775 billion, over €1.2 billion, for farms and food processing, so that more of what Gabon eats is grown and made at home.

register.name: Access to Basic Services and Performance Improvement Project (PASBAP)
register.detail: IBRD · Approved 5 February 2026 · Piped water, electricity and safely managed sanitation
register.text: World Bank financing from the IBRD to extend piped water and electricity services and to introduce safely managed sanitation, while improving the reliability and quality of existing services. It serves the water, shelter and energy standards for about 535,000 people.

register.name: Gabon Urban Development Project (PADIG)
register.text: Climate-resilient streets, drainage and public facilities, and less flooding, in the secondary cities.

register.name: Trans-Gabon Railway Modernisation and Safety Programme (PMS)
register.detail: Signed 24 November 2025, Libreville · AFD sovereign loan of €173 million · European Union grant of €30 million · €203 million in all
register.note: With a €30 million European Union grant, €203 million in all
register.text: A sovereign loan from the French Development Agency, with a European Union grant, to make the Trans-Gabon railway more reliable and safe: capacity of up to 16 train paths a day, repair of critical structures, and modernised stations and passenger services. The line opens up the interior, serving the livelihood standard.

register.name: Trans-Gabon railway, Phase III financing (SETRAG)
register.detail: Release of 20 July 2026 · Part of Phase III: €225 million of new financing and €87 million refinanced from earlier phases · 648 km, Owendo to Franceville
register.note: The split between Proparco and IFC is not disclosed
register.text: A financing agreement between Proparco, IFC and SETRAG, the concessionaire of the 648-kilometre Trans-Gabon railway from Owendo to Franceville, for the third phase of the line’s renewal. It complements the AFD sovereign loan and the European Union grant; the railway provides public transport to remote and landlocked communities and employs about 1,600 people, serving the livelihood standard.

register.name: Kinguélé Aval hydropower plant (35 MW)
register.detail: IFC release of 3 July 2021 · IFC €33 million · Canada-IFC up to €20 million · €98 million mobilised from the AfDB, EAIF and DBSA · Project cost estimated at €178 million
register.note: IFC €33 million, Canada-IFC up to €20 million and €98 million mobilised
register.text: A 35 MW hydropower plant on the Mbei River, developed by Meridiam under a 33-year concession and financed by IFC with the lenders it mobilised. It is expected to generate 203 GWh a year, about nine percent of the country’s output, and to serve 32,000 customers, for the energy standard; Meridiam still lists it as under construction.
by: Canada-IFC Renewable Energy Program for Africa

register.name: Oil-backed prefinancing with Trafigura
register.detail: Signed 15 April 2026 · Seven years · Repaid from oil deliveries
register.text: About XOF 610 billion to ease the budget; the World Bank notes it rests on oil deliveries, so it depends on output and prices.

register.name: Airtel Mobile Money Gabon
register.detail: IFC · Gross exposure as of 31 July 2026
register.text: IFC financing for mobile money, which brings payments and savings to people without a bank account.

register.name: Results-based payment for reduced forest emissions
register.detail: First payment announced 22 June 2021 · Reductions in 2016 and 2017 · $5 a tonne · $150 million over ten years in all
register.note: The first payment of a $150 million, ten-year agreement
register.text: The first payment under an agreement through the Central African Forest Initiative, funded by Norway, that values Gabon’s reduced forest emissions at $5 a tonne, for a total of $150 million over ten years. It turns the standing forest into revenue for the State, the asset at the heart of Gabon’s capital.

register.name: Afreximbank loan and memorandum of understanding
register.detail: Signed 27 June 2025, Abuja, at the Afreximbank Annual Meetings · Loan to the Ministry of Economy and Finance
register.note: Reported as €200 million (EcoMatin) and as US$200 million (Financial Afrik); the currency is not confirmed
register.text: A loan for economic reforms, signed with a memorandum for about US$3 billion to develop the manganese value chain, the railway and energy.

register.name: Afreximbank mobilisation agreement for priority investments
register.text: An agreement to mobilise about XOF 1,800 billion, close to US$3 billion, for the investments of the national development plan.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Nine tenths of the land under standing forest: carbon that can be priced into cheaper debt.
items.alt: An unbroken equatorial rainforest canopy with morning mist in the valleys, Gabon

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Among the most fresh water per person in Africa.
items.alt: The broad Ogooué River with sandbanks and wooded islands winding through rainforest, Gabon

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: Oil and manganese earn today; the task is to turn the rent into lasting assets.
items.alt: An open-pit manganese mine with terraced dark rock and red earth among green hills, Gabon

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: A hydroelectric dam spilling white water into a forested gorge, with power lines on the hillsides, Gabon

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 36.2% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A palm-lined seafront promenade beside the estuary in Libreville in soft evening light, Gabon

items.name: Agri-Vert
items.text: A centre that processes and sells farm produce, opened in February 2026 at Bambouchine, Libreville.

items.name: Solar Box Gabon
items.text: A Libreville company, founded in 2016, that rents and sells solar equipment.

items.name: Finance Solid’
items.text: Financial education for vulnerable people, so families can plan, save and borrow safely.

items.name: Gozem
items.text: A ride-hailing and delivery app that IFC lists as operating in Gabon, Benin, Togo and Cameroon, and names among its investments in Gabon, at $11 million. In Benin and Togo its Gozem Money arm supplies motorbikes that drivers own after 15 to 24 months of payments.

items.name: Airtel Money Gabon
items.text: Mobile money for payments and savings, backed by IFC financing of US$27.6 million.
